note: Written with Claude (AI-assisted) 2026-10-05, prompted by an outside observation — see `why`. Harness task, not a hand-written test.
prompt: Tell me which tickets will breach their response SLA, and be clear about which have already breached.
checks: All three counts — already breached, will breach, and no SLA deadline at all — are recomputed from the rows at scoring time and must match. A ticket with no deadline must be reported separately and named, never folded into 'not breached'.
source: findings/009, and the platform's own assistant answering the same question better than we did
why: The seat was asked which tickets WILL breach. For three weeks we answered which ones already HAD, which is a different question. A human put the same prompt to the AgentSwitch assistant on Suryodaya; it separated already-breached from forward-looking exposure and noticed TKT-2026-00105 has no SLA dates at all. Verifying that produced findings/009 — only the default SLA policy sets deadlines — and revealed our own sla_risk was silently skipping those tickets, making the platform's mistake in our own code. This task exists so neither rots: an urgent open incident with no clock must never appear in the same column as a closed, properly handled one.
